title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'troisième mouture' of Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs', an axiomatic, lattice-theoretic approach to tame or stratified topology. The basic objects are a lattice of 'supports' (closed-type parts of a space M) and a sublattice L. Each part has a support (supp) and a cosupport. Each 'cell' X has an interior X°, a boundary ∂X and an associated open 'ouvb(X)'. The axioms are labelled AtL1, AtL2, AtL3.

Previous page: Grothendieck finds a counterexample in a small graph (a chain A'–A–B–B') to a lemma he had hoped for. He concludes that some extra axiom would be needed, e.g. S_{A−B} = S_A ∩ ∁S_B, which he suspects holds for 'varieties' under a divisibility-type hypothesis. That hypothesis is the one used to give intrinsic meaning to 'constructible supports' via the X°. The first two lines of this page finish that sentence.

26 June entry, first part (simplifying a definition). Since he is in practice forced to assume AtL1 (besides AtL2 and AtL3) in order to define X° for 'supports' in his 'parallel' sense ('||'), he proposes to define the interior directly as X° = Supp(ouvb(X)°). He says this agrees with the earlier definition by the arguments of p. 86, together with a consequence of AtL2:
- every 'supporting' part S of M satisfies S = supp(S ∩ L);
- more generally, for any S, supp S = Supp(S ∩ L).
In words, supports are determined by their trace on the distinguished sublattice L. The line 'pour ≪, ...' is left unfinished.

Lemma (stated 'pour nous rassurer', i.e. as a sanity check):
- Let F ≼ X. On the next page this is recalled to mean that F refines X (F ≪ X) with the same support.
- Let φ: F̃ → X̃ be the induced map on cells.
- Put F̃° = φ^{-1}({X}) = {X' ∈ F̃ : X'° ⊂ X°}, the cells of the refinement whose interiors lie in the interior of X.
- Claim: X° = Sup_Σ over X' ∈ F̃° of X'°, i.e. X° = Supp(⋃ X'°) = Supp(⋃ ouvb(X')°).

Modern reading: when a cell or stratified decomposition is refined, the open cell (stratum) of X is, up to taking the support/closure operation, the union of the open cells of the refinement that map to it. Equivalently, strata of a refinement partition the strata of the coarser decomposition.

Proof sketch begun on this page: treat the 'ensembliste' (set-theoretic) case. The inclusion ⊃ is clear because each X'° ⊂ X°. The inclusion ⊂ is reduced to a statement continued on the next page. There he introduces a support function |·| with values in a set P (conditions SUPP1, SUPP2) and shows |X°| = |X| \ |∂X|, so that F̃° consists of the X' with |X'°| disjoint from |∂X|.
errors: No outright mathematical error on this page. The proof of the inclusion ⊂ is left unfinished here and is only partly carried out on the next page.

The claimed equivalence of the new definition X° = Supp ouvb(X)° with the earlier one rests on unstated 'arguments p. 86' and on AtL1, which Grothendieck admits he is forced to assume. The previous page shows that his earlier axioms were insufficient, so the logical status of the system remains provisional.
In the lemma, the identification φ^{-1}({X}) = {X' : X'° ⊂ X°} is an implicit claim about the map φ, not proved here.

ideas.what: Define the interior of a cell as the support of the interior of its associated open set, X° = Supp ouvb(X)°, using axiom AtL1.
ideas.modern_name: interior/open stratum in an axiomatic (lattice-theoretic) framework for stratified or tame spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stratification theory: Whitney, Thom, Mather; o-minimality: van den Dries; Grothendieck's Esquisse programme of 'tame topology'
ideas.where_published: Only the general wish for a 'topologie modérée' appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); these axioms are unpublished

ideas.what: Every supporting part S satisfies S = supp(S ∩ L), and in general supp S = Supp(S ∩ L): supports are determined by their trace on the distinguished sublattice L.
ideas.modern_name: density / generation of a lattice of closed sets by a sublattice

ideas.what: Lemma: for a refinement F ≼ X (same support), X° is the support-sup of the interiors of the refining cells that map to X.
ideas.modern_name: strata of a refinement partition the strata of the coarser stratification (cell-decomposition compatibility)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in CW-complex, stratification and o-minimal cell decomposition theory

missed.claim: This is part of Grothendieck's unpublished attempt at a purely lattice-theoretic axiomatics of 'analysis situs' (supports, cosupports, interiors, boundaries, refinements, axioms AtL1–3, SUPP1–2), meant to give an intrinsic meaning to 'constructible supports'. The axiom system is visibly in flux: a lemma failed on the previous page and AtL1 is added here. No one appears to have completed or published such an axiomatics in this form.
missed.quote: pratiquement je suis obligé ici ... d'admettre AtL1 (en plus de AtL2, AtL3)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may be of modest interest for comparing with point-free and lattice-theoretic approaches to o-minimal or tame topology, and with abstract stratified-space formalisms. The content of this specific page is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step (a redefinition of interiors and a sanity-check lemma on refinements) inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology project. The broader project is little known, but nothing on this page would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The next page's number '200' is almost certainly '100'.

The line under the lemma's equality reads roughly 'Prouvons, dans le cas d'un genre ensembliste, ...'. The following phrase ('en écrivant au général par') is uncertain. The formula there is ouvb(X)° = ⋃_{X'∈F̃°} ouvb(X')°, where the subscript '*' is doubtful.
The added note above the set-builder is 'i.e. X'° ⊂ X°'.
The crossed-out 'Donc' at the bottom is followed by 'Cela équivaut au', which continues onto the next page.
